opex.name: Technology and development
opex.note: Building and running the app and its trading systems.

opex.name: Provision for credit losses
opex.note: Money set aside for customer loans that may not be repaid.

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and promotions to win new customers.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Legal, finance, compliance and running the company — swollen this quarter by acquisition-related costs.

follow100Note: Robinhood kept $47.16 of every $100 — a very different business from a retailer: most revenue arrives as fees and interest, and the biggest costs are engineers and growth spending. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Robinhood does not report a separate cost of revenue; 'Brokerage and transaction' — the direct cost of executing customers' trades — is shown as the direct cost here. Net income of $605M is attributable to Robinhood; there was no non-controlling interest this quarter.

kpis.label: EPS (diluted)
kpis.note: vs $1.01 a year ago, which included a $0.47 one-time benefit

oneTimers: The year-ago comparison is flattered by a $424M benefit in Q4 2024 — a deferred-tax benefit plus the reversal of a regulatory accrual — worth $0.47 of that quarter's $1.01 EPS. Q4 2025 has no equivalent item.

General and administrative costs jumped 154% to $178M, driven by acquisition-related expenses for the TradePMR and Bitstamp deals and by growth investments; total operating expenses rose 38% to $633M.
otherDetail: Other income (loss), net was $11M — small next to the main business.

segments.name: Transaction-based revenues
segments.note: Fees from customers' trades — options brought in $314M, crypto $221M, equities $94M, and other transaction revenue, including event contracts, jumped over 300% to $147M.

segments.name: Net interest revenues
segments.note: Interest on customers' cash and margin loans, plus securities lending — up 39% as balances grew.

segments.name: Other revenues
segments.note: Mostly Robinhood Gold subscriptions — $50M, up 56% — plus other services.

takeaways.text: Total Platform Assets rose 68% to $324B, with $15.9B of net deposits in the quarter alone and $68.1B over the year. Funded customers reached 27.0M.
takeaways.title: Customers keep piling in assets

takeaways.text: Robinhood Gold subscribers rose 58% to a record 4.2M, and Gold subscription revenue rose 56% to $50M — part of why 'other revenues' more than doubled to $96M.
takeaways.title: Gold becomes a real business

takeaways.text: Net income fell from $916M to $605M, but last year's quarter included a $424M benefit from a deferred-tax item and a reversed regulatory accrual. Underneath, revenue grew 27%.
takeaways.title: Profit is down — on paper

verdict: Robinhood's revenue rose 27% to $1.28B as options trading and interest income grew — and its $605M profit only looks down 34% because a year ago included a $424M one-time tax and regulatory benefit.
